body:
`case_study:balkrishna-industries-2009-2024` · tickers: BALKRISIND · confidence: verified

Split-adjusted ₹12.4 (Mar 2009) → ₹3,292 (Aug 2024) ≈266x; ₹2,327 on 19 Nov 2026 (−29%). Twin engine: trailing P/E ~2.2 at the Mar 2009 trough (TTM EPS ₹5.7) → 48.6, about 22x rerating × implied EPS ~12x. About 55% of the log-return was the multiple, the highest share among the long-duration cases here. Drawdowns: −89% (2006–09, before), −34% (2013), −32% (2014–16), −48% (2018–19), −39% (2024–26). Early signal: a niche global off-highway (agri, OTR) replacement-tyre exporter (~85–90% exports, Europe the largest market) priced like a commodity truck-tyre maker; P/E 6–13 through 2010–2015 while EPS compounded; Bhuj greenfield plant (first tyre 2012, completed ~2015) roughly doubling capacity to ~300k t. Investors who saw 'global niche, Indian cost base' held a 9-year rerating to 24–36x by 2017–2021. Stalled: EPS flat FY22–26 (~₹74), ROCE down from ~24% to ~11% after heavy capex (carbon black, Bhuj expansions), weak European agri demand and freight. Lesson: the biggest rerating wins come from a market's mis-classification (commodity → niche franchise); when returns on capital fall, the rerating stops.

Key data: **start_year**: 2009; **end_year**: 2024; **start_price**: 12.4; **end_price**: 3292; **price_nov2026**: 2327; **multiple**: ~266x; **pe_start**: 2.2; **pe_end**: 48.6; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~12x; **max_drawdown**: -48% (2018-19); **early_signals**: niche global OHT exporter at P/E 2-6; capacity doubling at Bhuj; **ended**: ROCE 24%→11%, EPS flat FY22-26; **lesson**: mis-classification rerating; watch ROCE after big capex

Sources: <https://www.screener.in/company/BALKRISIND/consolidated/> · <https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/off-highway-business-keeps-balkrishna-in-fast-lane-116112901460_1.html> · <https://www.outlookbusiness.com/feature/all-set-for-the-big-leap-786> · <https://www.farmersjournal.ie/machinery/farm-machinery/bkt-the-tyre-manufacturer-producing-1-3m-tyres-annually-853899>

India has more promoter/group leverage (holdco debt, pledges), more IBC cases, and negative equity is rarely buyback-driven
(buybacks are small), so the exemption will hardly ever apply. We need a point-in-time universe with dead companies
(IBC admissions from IBBI, NSE/BSE delistings and suspensions) — Pi/Screener data. Re-test S1, S5 and an ALM/short-term
gap version for NBFCs separately (excluded here). Thresholds may differ: Indian interest cover is lower across the board at
higher rates.

Scripts: `tools/backtests/solvency_us/` (common, s1_candidates, s2_fetch, s3_flags, s4_events, s4b_item301_text,
s5_prices, s6_analyze). Outputs: `research_notes/Backtests/solvency_us_outputs/` (panel.csv, results.json, tables.md,
funnel.json). Raw cache in the session scratchpad `bt_solvency/` (not durable).

body:
**Inputs (L8 step 1):** close ₹355.85 on 23-Nov-2026 (NSE bhavcopy; screener ₹356 — two sources; Yahoo has no bar after 18-Nov, ₹358.00); 10 FY-end
P/Es FY17–26 (18.6, 21.1, 12.4, 7.1, 214.8, 9.1, 8.2, 12.7, 22.0, 18.6; median 15.7); peers 33.3–58.8 (median 48.0); 6-month ADV ₹11.6 cr mean /
₹5.5 cr median `[YH]`; net cash ₹521.4 cr; no pending dilution.
**Scenarios (written before the outputs; legal outcome over 5 years):** blow-up 20% (non-renewal/handover → ~0.25x: net cash ₹57/share plus uncertain
compensation for the building/equipment); bear 20% (renewal with enforced 33%/40% EWS incl. medicines and/or market rent: revenue −8% then +5%,
NOPAT margin → 5%, exit 14x); base 45% (pendency continues or renewal on IMCL's ask: +9% → +7%, NOPAT margin 11.2% → 10%, ROIIC 30%, exit 20x); bull
15% (30-year renewal near current terms, partial re-rating: +11%, 12%, exit 28x).
**Outputs:** 5-year multiples bear 0.59x / base 1.70x / bull 2.74x / blow-up 0.25x; **EV 1.35x raw** vs hurdle 1.76x; P(≥2x) 26%, P(≥3x) 7%, P(≤0.5x)
26%, P(blow-up) 20%. Base-case IRR **10.9%** vs CoE 12.5%. Probability-weighted DCF ₹235 (−34%). Reverse DCF: flat margin needs 11.0% revenue
CAGR for 10 years — close to recent growth, *if the hospital is kept*.
**Exit-multiple bet:** DCF-consistent exit P/E 14.7–16.1 vs used 14/20/28 vs own median 15.7 → EV 1.35x / 0.99x / 1.02x. As in every card so far
(L21, L36) the exit multiple is the binding choice; here it is also a proxy for the legal outcome (peers' 48x is what "kept the hospital" might fetch).
**Temperature:** 17.0x = NORMAL vs own history (1.09x median; the own history spans the dormant-dispute, low-margin years), **COLD vs sector (0.35x)**.
**Price-implied probability (two-state read) `[EST]`:** going concern at ~30x on ₹192 cr PAT + cash ≈ ₹630/share; handover ≈ ₹60–90/share. ₹356
implies **P(workable renewal) ≈ 50%**. We have no basis to say the market's ~50% is wrong.
